note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Situated embedding: motivation, design, and evidence

nodes.name: Chunk meaning depends on context
nodes.description: Documents have narrative or logical flow, so the meaning of each chunk depends heavily on its surrounding context, creating a need for context-aware embeddings.

nodes.name: Embedding capacity limits long chunks
nodes.description: Embedding models must compress a chunk into one vector, so longer chunks raise the chance of critical information loss; applications built on long-chunk embeddings often underperform those using short chunks.

nodes.name: Recall drops with longer chunks
nodes.description: On the book plot retrieval task, with the same total returned text (5k/10k/25k tokens) and the same embedding model (Jina or NV-Embed), recall consistently decreases as documents are segmented into longer chunks.

nodes.name: Situated embedding approach
nodes.description: Situated embedding conditions a short chunk's embedding on its broader context, so the model only needs to integrate context relevant to the target chunk, easing the capacity limit.

nodes.name: Existing models lack zero-shot situated embedding
nodes.description: Adding situated context to chunks significantly degrades the recall of all tested existing embedding models (M3, Jina-v3, E5-Mistral, GTE-Qwen2, NV-Embed-v2, Qwen3-Embedding) on NDP-v1, even though the context is within their claimed context windows (e.g. Jina-v3 Recall@10 53.33 chunk-only vs 15.68 with context).

nodes.name: Failure partly from long-input weakness
nodes.description: Replacing situated context with GPT-4o-generated situated summaries yields much smaller degradation or slight gains for M3, Jina, E5 and Qwen3, indicating the baselines partly fail to situate a chunk within long contexts.

nodes.name: Book-note training data
nodes.description: Training data is built from ~1.6M (1,614,007) query-chunk pairs of user book notes (Douban, ~100 popular books), treating the note as query and its anchored text as the chunk, since notes reflect contextual understanding.

nodes.name: Residual learning architecture
nodes.description: The situated model learns the residual over a baseline chunk-only embedding model (query q~ = qb + qs, chunk c~ = cb + cs), with a margin loss over 10 negatives, to prevent shortcut use of ambiguous chunk-only clues and encourage context use.

nodes.name: SitEmb-v1 outperforms larger models
nodes.description: SitEmb-v1-M3 (1B) with situated context reaches Recall@10 of 50.85 on NDP-v1, exceeding chunk-only M3 (42.55) and outperforming models up to 7B parameters.

nodes.name: SitEmb-v1.5 further gains
nodes.description: SitEmb-v1.5-Qwen3 (8B) with book-note data reaches Recall@10 of 68.98 on NDP-v1, above voyage-context-3 (60.46) and Qwen3-Embedding chunk-only (51.58).

nodes.name: No training-test overlap effect
nodes.description: Including NDP books in NarrativeQA-based training gives no measurable gain on NDP-v1 (Recall@10 68.98 w/ vs 69.60 w/o), so book overlap does not drive results.

nodes.name: Robust to context length
nodes.description: SitEmb performance on NDP-v1 is stable across situated context lengths from 512-800 to 8192-12800 tokens.

nodes.name: Full plot retrieval improvement
nodes.description: On the full book plot retrieval task (7 books, 1,394 queries), SitEmb-v1.5-Qwen3 improves by over 10% when trained on QA data and over 15% on QA+SA data, and both exceed voyage-context-3 (Recall@10 63.03 for QA+SA vs 51.39).

nodes.name: Residual architecture is not capacity gain
nodes.description: Training the same residual architecture on chunk-only M3 (Res-M3) does not improve over M3 (SA), and removing residual learning degrades SitEmb-v1-M3, indicating gains come from using contextual information.

nodes.name: Recap identification generalization
nodes.description: On Recap Snippet Identification, SitEmb-v1.5 (QA+SA) is best (F1@5 38.9 vs 37.9 for Qwen3), while models trained without context usage drop slightly.

nodes.name: Story QA downstream gains
nodes.description: SitEmb-v1.5 (QA) outperforms its no-context counterpart on story understanding tasks (NarrativeQA, InfBench MC, DetectiveQA, NoCha) except on LongStoryQA, and substantially beats out-of-box Qwen3 especially at top-3 and top-5.

nodes.name: QA vs SA complementary strengths
nodes.description: On DetectiveQA, SitEmb (QA) has the highest answer-evidence recall (top-3 42.5) and SitEmb (QA+SA) the highest clue-evidence recall (top-3 26.9), reflecting semantic association ability.

isolated_nodes.name: Evaluation dataset
isolated_nodes.description: The Book Plot Retrieval task repurposes PlotRetrieval into chunk-level retrieval over 7 books (each >100,000 tokens) with 1,394 queries, reporting Recall@10/20/50.

isolated_nodes.name: Plot retrieval needs localized results
isolated_nodes.description: Users recalling a plot need localized short evidence (each segment about 2-3 pages), so returning long chunks is not an option.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from the context-dependence and capacity problem, through situated embedding and residual-training design, to evidence that existing models fail and SitEmb succeeds, with robustness and downstream results.
